text: The Health Ministry said Monday it had ordered the nationwide withdrawal of Zenthora cough syrup after tests confirmed the product’s active ingredient was guaifenol, not the decongestant compound listed on its label. In a notice citing the ministry’s Therapeutics Safety Bureau, officials said the discrepancy emerged during a routine inspection of Solmere Laboratories’ batch 24Z-18, manufactured in March and distributed to pharmacies in six provinces. Dr. Leona Vesk, head of the bureau, said the label error posed “a material risk of misuse” because dosing guidance had been written for a different formulation. Solmere said it was recalling remaining stock and cooperating with investigators. No injuries have been reported, the ministry said.
